definition: Reducing the numeric precision of a model’s weights (e.g. from 16-bit to 8-bit or 4-bit) to cut memory and speed inference.
details: Quantization maps continuous weights to a small set of discrete values. LLM.int8() showed that 8-bit inference could run large Transformers without degradation by separating outlier dimensions, which appear at scale, from the rest of the activations. Lower-bit formats (4-bit) are now routine for running large models on consumer hardware.

explainer.lead: Quantization lowers the numeric precision of a model's weights, for example from 16-bit to 8-bit or 4-bit, to cut memory use and speed inference. It matters because it makes large models runnable on ordinary hardware.

tiers.eli5: Storing prices rounded to whole dollars instead of cents — the numbers take less space, and usually the total is close enough.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers map continuous weights to a small set of discrete values before deployment. A known pitfall is outlier dimensions: at scale these appear in activations and must be handled separately or accuracy drops.
tiers.paperLevel: Quantization maps continuous weights to a small discrete set; LLM.int8() showed 8-bit inference could run large Transformers without degradation by separating outlier dimensions from the rest of the activations, and 4-bit formats are now routine.

explainer.example: LLM.int8() runs large Transformer models in 8-bit without degradation by isolating outlier activation dimensions, and 4-bit formats run large models on consumer hardware.

citation.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS)
